text:
maya: Quick question — thinking about how we split collector responsibilities. Agents are seeing spikes (SDKs emitting ~10k traces/s) and we hit memory pressure when we try to do buffering + disk spill on the agent. Should we: 1) keep agents very thin (forward-only, maybe sampling), 2) push buffering/retention/exporter heavy-lifting to a gateway, or 3) do per-signal pipelines on the agent (separate traces/logs pipelines) to limit OOMs? Looking for tradeoffs and concrete config patterns.
ashwin: We've hit agent OOMs before when logs + spans were in same pipeline. Separate pipelines per signal (trace vs logs) bought us immediate wins. Also add memory_limiter ext/processor.
tristan: +1 to thin agents that forward. Gateway can do disk-backed exporters and aggregate/rollup. But note: adds an extra network hop and TLS costs. For latency-sensitive traces that might matter.
sophia: Sampling at the agent is a powerful lever — cut incoming volume early. But it changes evals/QA and affects downstream metrics. If we sample, keep deterministic sampling keys and signal-path tags.
kai: For multi-tenant routing we should do per-tenant pipelines in gateway so retention/TTL/compliance can differ by customer. Agents shouldn't hold tenant policy logic.
maya: Any examples of a minimal agent config vs a gateway config? Particularly around disk-backed exporters or file-based buffering.
nashwin: Here's a simplified OTEL collector idea we used in staging (very condensed):

```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}

extensions:
  health_check: {}
  pprof: {}
  file_storage:
    directory: /var/lib/otel-queue

processors:
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 10s
    limit_mib: 512
  batch:
    timeout: 200ms

exporters:
  otlp/http/gateway:
    endpoint: gateway.local:4318
  file_spill:
    path: /var/lib/otel-queue/spill.json

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/http/gateway, file_spill]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter]
      exporters: [otlp/http/gateway]
  extensions: [health_check, file_storage]
```

This is an agent that forwards to a gateway but also writes to a local file exporter for spill. In prod we prefer the gateway to own the disk-backed exporter with persistent storage and TTL/compaction.
tristan: Gateway strategy: run per-signal pipelines, disk-backed queue + compaction, and exporter adapters that can batch aggressively. Also implement backpressure to agents if gateway is unhealthy.
infra-bot: ALERT: otel-agent-memory > 75% in prod cluster us-east-2 (last 24h spikes). Suggesting immediate mitigation via sampling or route-to-gateway.
sophia: Another pattern: lightweight agent does deterministic head-based sampling + extract important attributes, gateway does tail-sampling/advanced sampling and enrichment before export.
kai: For retention, gateway can apply TTLs per signal and tenant and surface a metrics-only export path (rollups) to long-term storage while evicting raw spans sooner.
tristan: Tradeoffs to call out in RFC: extra hop latency, TLS CPU, serialization cost, more moving parts to manage. Upsides: central place for retention, per-tenant policy, easier debug, and better disk/buffer guarantees.
maya: My current proposal draft: agents = minimal transforms + deterministic sampling + secure forward; gateway = per-signal pipelines, disk-backed exporters, per-tenant retention/rollup, and export retries. Will sketch an RFC with perf numbers and suggested defaults (agent memory limiter = 512MiB, gateway disk queue cap = 100GiB, default sample rate = 0.1 for high-volume SDKs).
nashwin: ++ include a migration plan: feature flags to flip sampling and a canary gateway fleet. Also add alerts for agent memory, agent-to-gateway drop rate, and gateway queue depth.
sophia: Add one test: replay 1M spans/min into a staging agent -> gateway path and measure end-to-end tail latency and percent of spans spilled to disk.
maya: Thanks — I'll post RFC by EOD and link the perf test infra. Ping me if you want specific test scenarios added. :raised_hands!
